# maystash

> Personal site of May — long-form, reproducible writing on AI agents, second brains
> (persistent AI memory systems), security, and building products from zero.
> Every article is a complete blueprint: frameworks, templates, and copy-paste starter kits.
> Plain-markdown source, no paywall, no gating.

## Posts

- [The AI Memory Everyone's Building Is a Diary. Here's How to Build a Brain That Sleeps.](https://maystash.xyz/posts/brain-that-sleeps/):
  Seven primitives for a self-improving AI second brain on plain text files — index-first
  retrieval, verified/guess tagging, rule distillation, git as memory versioning, a weekly
  "dreaming" consolidation pass, memory-poisoning defenses, and a copy-paste starter kit.

- [Your Burger Drinks More Than Your Chatbot. So Why Are the Wells Running Dry?](https://maystash.xyz/posts/thirsty-machines/):
  Plain-language one-stop guide to AI and water. What an AI prompt actually costs (a few
  drops to a shot glass, depending which "fence" you measure), how it compares to burgers
  (~2,500 L), jeans, coffee, and golf (US golf out-drinks all US data centers ~30x); the
  three measurement boundaries that explain why estimates vary 2,000x; per-model disclosure
  scoreboard (Gemini and Mistral disclose, OpenAI barely, Anthropic/Meta/xAI/DeepSeek not
  at all); what Microsoft/Google/AWS/Meta/xAI are doing to mitigate; and why data-center
  neighbors (The Dalles, West Des Moines, Newton County, Memphis, Tucson) are right to worry
  even though nationally AI water use is a rounding error. First post in the Matinee section.

- [Your AI Agent Doesn't Need More Autonomy. It Needs a Leash With Six Knots.](https://maystash.xyz/posts/agents-need-a-leash/):
  The six-clause contract every recurring AI job (a "loop") should sign before it runs
  unsupervised — explicit schedule, one changed variable per round, a versioned metric,
  a state file (with the watchdog trick: a stale last_run means silent death), three hard
  stops (done condition, blocked condition that halts and logs instead of retrying, and a
  budget cap), and an independent verifier so the context that produced the work never
  grades it. Golden rule: a loop automates a motion you already do well by hand, never
  invents one, and loops draft/flag while humans keep publish and delete. Includes a
  20-minute setup checklist.

- [One of Our Players Never Lost. That Wasn't Skill — It Was Our Bug.](https://maystash.xyz/posts/player-who-never-lost/):
  Plain-language case study of two cheats against a daily number-puzzle game (Dinjure) and
  the fixes. Cheat one: the daily secret was derived by client-side code shipped to every
  browser, so anyone reading the page source could compute the answer and "solve" in one
  guess — fixed by moving secret generation and answer-checking to the server so the client
  never holds the answer. Cheat two: unlimited free anonymous accounts plus an end-of-game
  answer reveal let a player scout the code on a throwaway account, then solve on their real
  one — caught by timestamp patterns (the clincher: the throwaway lost and the real account
  still solved perfectly), fixed server-side by excluding the affected scores from ranking
  rather than banning. Detection logic deliberately unpublished. Lessons: anything sent to
  the client is readable, frictionless free access is also free abuse surface, cheating is
  usually unwatched rather than invisible, and demoting beats punishing. Matinee section.
